html:
SMTO-EXE-0136 — A file download in the web browser failed

GUID: 265f80a4-a1f5-5edc-803c-0427c4325390
Slug: browser-download-failed
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • The website started a download, but the web browser reported that it failed before the file was complete. No file was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the same website yourself and check that the download works there. If it fails for you too, the problem is with the website or the file, not with SMTO.
  2. Ask SMTO to look at the page and its list of downloads and tell you what they show. The page may show a reason, such as needing to sign in or the file no longer being available.
  3. When the cause is fixed, ask SMTO plainly to start the download one more time. SMTO never repeats a download on its own, so it needs you to ask.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the download as completed and gives you the file.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the website address, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't share your website password or saved browser sign-ins to get around the failure.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The browser's download handle reported failure, or produced no file path, before export could return a verified file.

What this means

  • The retained browser download handle reported failure before export could produce a verified file result. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • The retained browser download handle reported failure before export could produce a verified file result.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact retained download and current page/source state, distinguishing download failure from later artifact publication failure.

How to fix it

  • Inspect browser.downloads (state failed) and the page with browser.snapshot to find the cause, such as a network error, a site-side cancellation or required sign-in. Fix the source, then start a new download only when the user explicitly asks; the backend never retries downloads.
  • Inspect browser.downloads and page state. Resolve the download source before an explicitly authorized retry.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect browser.downloads and page state. Resolve the download source before an explicitly authorized retry.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate justified download obtains a successful retained result before export.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
